title: Gravity Atlas
archiveRole: First Physics Experiment Hall observation sample
description: A PC-first deterministic physics puzzle. Drag from the launch pad to aim and fire a probe across six gravity plates, curving its path through masses, repulsors, and void zones into the target ring within each plate's shot budget. The physics engine is a shared pure module, and a committed Node verifier replays embedded reference launch vectors to prove every plate is completable.

deviceSupport.mobileNotes: PC-first physics benchmark tuned for mouse aiming at 1440x900 and 1920x1080. Mobile is a no-overflow baseline: the 16:9 plate scales to width and drag-aiming works as a touch gesture, but fine trajectory control is intended for a mouse. Interactive browser smoke and physical handset QA are pending and not claimed.

provenance.notes: Model label is maintainer-declared for this project entry. The deterministic physics engine, plate designs, embedded reference solutions, and the standing Node verifier were authored by Claude Code under the no-human-code-edits project rule.

pointer: Drag on the plate to aim and set power, release to fire
keyboard: Arrow keys for fine aim and power
touch: Drag on the plate to aim, lift to fire

verification.completabilityProof: node scripts/verify-gravity-atlas.mjs replays the reference launch vectors embedded in src/engine.js through the same fixed-timestep engine the browser runs and asserts every plate ends in a target hit within its shot budget.

repositoryNote: Observation 005 / Game 005. First Physics Experiment Hall benchmark: simulation feel, spatial reasoning, cause/effect readability, and a machine-verifiable completability proof.
